sentences.quote: QXO, Inc. (NYSE: QXO), today announced the appointment of Ken West as President and Chief Operating Officer, effective September 1, 2026. West will report to Chief Executive Officer Brad Jacobs
sentences.text: QXO appointed Ken West, previously president and chief executive of Honeywell Process Technology, as president and chief operating officer effective September 1, 2026, reporting to chief executive Brad Jacobs and responsible for day-to-day operations; Jacobs called him "an exceptional operator" whose leadership would help scale the platform.

Madeline Otero became interim chief accounting officer on July 1, 2026, replacing Robert Loughran, interim holder since March 15, 2026, and Jared Kushner resigned from the board effective July 1, 2026.

sentences.quote: QXO to Become the Second Largest Publicly Traded Building Products Distributor in North America, with More Than $18 Billion of Combined Company Revenue and More Than $2 Billion of Combined Company Adjusted EBITDA
sentences.text: The $17 billion TopBuild acquisition creates the second largest publicly traded building products distributor in North America, with more than $18 billion of combined revenue and over $2 billion of combined adjusted EBITDA, adding higher-margin insulation to roofing, waterproofing and lumber.
Management is led by Brad Jacobs, who previously built XPO, GXO, RXO, United Rentals and United Waste Systems, with a team experienced in large-scale integration.
Demand drivers include a shortage of about 4 million U.S. homes and aged housing stock requiring repair and remodeling.

thesis_pillars.text: Completed deals have built scale quickly: Kodiak Building Partners closed in April 2026 for about $2.25 billion, lifting QXO's addressable market above $200 billion, against a stated goal of $50 billion in annual revenue. The $17 billion TopBuild acquisition creates the second largest publicly traded building products distributor in North America, with more than $18 billion of combined revenue and over $2 billion of combined adjusted EBITDA, adding higher-margin insulation to roofing, waterproofing and lumber.
